name: Marianne Alto

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on re-election launch

biography: Alto has served as Victoria's mayor since 2022, after serving as a city councillor from 2010 to 2022. Her City biography describes a background in facilitation, university training in law and science, and work on housing, community wellbeing and relations with the Songhees and Xwsepsum Nations.

photo.alt: Mayor Marianne Alto wearing a hard hat outdoors

platform.summary: She identifies renter protection and housing affordability as priorities for another term.
She describes a prevention, intervention and response approach to community safety and wellbeing.
Her launch also identifies sustained arts and culture funding and protection of parks as priorities.
She says another term would include maintaining a responsible municipal budget.

name: Lyall Atkinson
biography: Atkinson is publicly listed for the 2026 Victoria mayoral race by Livable CRD. He was also a candidate for mayor in Victoria's 2022 election and appears in the City's official results for that election.

photo.alt: Lyall Atkinson outside Victoria City Hall

name: Bruce McGuigan
biography: McGuigan's campaign describes a career in education, community development, public service and social innovation, including work as a university professor and leader of non-profit organizations. He previously ran for Victoria mayor in 2018.

photo.alt: Bruce McGuigan, right, with David Lau outside the Victoria Social Innovation Centre

platform.summary: He calls for coordinated housing, health, treatment and recovery systems aimed at making homelessness rare, brief and non-recurring.
He supports market and non-market housing, family-sized rentals, affordable ownership paths and protection of existing lower-cost rentals.
He proposes open decision-making, understandable budgets, transparent contracts and earlier, continuous public consultation.
He supports policing and enforcement alongside prevention, public-space design, civilian and health responses, and action on homelessness and addiction.
He proposes stronger City partnership with local businesses, a continuing buy-local campaign and procurement that keeps more spending in the community.
He supports practical climate-resilience work on buildings, extreme heat, smoke, water, food security, transit and active transportation.
He says Victoria should support conditions in which artists and cultural organizations can live, work and create.

name: Matthew Schryer
biography: Schryer is publicly listed for the 2026 Victoria mayoral race by Livable CRD. His campaign Instagram identifies him as a candidate for mayor of Victoria in 2026.

name: Wendy Bowkett
biography: Bowkett is a business strategist with an MBA and a former leader of the Victoria Downtown Residents Association. Her campaign biography also notes board service with the 9-10 Club Soup Kitchen.

platform.summary: She proposes clearer public reporting and more meaningful engagement around council decisions.
She calls for a properly resourced safety system that includes non-police crisis response.
She supports faster approvals for non-market and co-op housing, paired with updated local area plans.

name: Jeremy Caradonna

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on re-election announcement

biography: Caradonna has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. His City biography describes him as a historian, professor and small-business owner who has worked on provincial climate and green-building policy.

photo.alt: Official portrait of Councillor Jeremy Caradonna

platform.summary: His re-election announcement identifies community safety as a developing campaign priority.
He identifies affordable housing and sustainable urban development as parts of his developing platform.
He proposes a municipal waste utility to provide garbage, recycling and compost collection across building types and institutions.
He supports examining regional rail and transit potential through the Capital Regional District.

name: Melissa Cseszko
biography: Cseszko describes herself as born and raised in Victoria and as a downtown small-business owner for five years. Her campaign frames that experience as the basis for a focus on downtown conditions and municipal accountability.

platform.summary: She emphasizes predictable, orderly downtown conditions and support for local businesses.
She calls for stronger oversight, performance measurement and accountability at City Hall.
Her campaign says heritage buildings and the character of established streets should be protected as the city changes.

name: Matt Dell
biography: Dell has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. His campaign biography describes a career in provincial policy, community volunteering, neighbourhood-association leadership and music, as well as a master's degree in political science.

photo.alt: Official portrait of Councillor Matt Dell

platform.summary: He lists building more homes as a central campaign priority.
He supports climate-ready parks and trees, repaired streets and sidewalks, and more walkable connected neighbourhoods.
He advocates for a new downtown public library, community events and continued investment in arts and culture.

name: Shona Dion
biography: Dion describes herself as a labour activist, community builder and photographer, and as a 28-year union member. Her campaign biography lists roles with the Victoria Labour Council and the North Jubilee Neighbourhood Association.

platform.summary: She supports social and co-operative housing and stronger health and safety protections for tenants.
She proposes heat-mitigation measures, more tree canopy and community gardens, and opposition to energy-intensive AI data centres.
She states support for bicycle infrastructure as part of a safer transportation network.

name: Jerry Garcia
biography: Garcia describes himself as a retired professional engineer, executive, entrepreneur and community volunteer with more than 40 years of experience on complex projects. His campaign says he has lived in downtown Victoria for eight years.

platform.summary: He says the City should strengthen economic growth and improve conditions for downtown residents and businesses.
His platform identifies restoring public safety as a priority.
He calls for fiscal responsibility and performance-focused municipal management.
He proposes a public scorecard for major City initiatives so residents can track goals and results.

name: Marg Gardiner
biography: Gardiner has served on Victoria City Council since 2022 and previously spent 16 years with the James Bay Neighbourhood Association. Her campaign biography lists degrees in chemistry and public administration and a professional background in regulation and data management.

platform.summary: She calls for adequate police resources, safer streets and a treatment-oriented response to addiction.
She proposes zero-based budgeting and measurable results for municipal spending.
She opposes the City's Missing Middle policy and current Official Community Plan density approach, favouring neighbourhood-scale planning.
She calls for greater transparency, public input and scrutiny of municipal spending to rebuild public confidence.

name: Peter Rose Gibbs

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on Victoria For All launch

biography: Rose Gibbs is a lifelong Victoria resident and parent whose campaign biography describes two decades of public advocacy. He is one of two City council candidates presented by Victoria For All at its August launch.

photo.alt: Campaign portrait of Peter Rose Gibbs

platform.summary: Victoria For All proposes doubling City investment in affordable housing; Rose Gibbs appears as a candidate on the organization's shared platform.
The organization's shared platform calls for expanded mental-health and addiction crisis response.
The shared platform proposes free, year-round and accessible community gathering spaces.

name: Martin Girard
biography: Girard is a Victoria resident and public advocate who has addressed City Council on civic issues. His campaign website presents a detailed platform centred on drug policy, human rights and Indigenous relations.

platform.summary: He advocates municipal decriminalization of simple drug possession and licensed compassion clubs within a public-health approach.
He proposes that the City advocate for Indigenous rights and support legal arguments grounded in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
His platform calls for the City to take public positions on selected international human-rights issues.

name: Stephen Hammond
biography: Hammond has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. His City biography describes him as a lawyer, professional speaker and author with experience on community boards.

photo.alt: Official portrait of Councillor Stephen Hammond

platform.summary: He makes a safer city a headline re-election priority.
He says recent property-tax increases are unsustainable, cites his votes against the last three budgets and calls for more disciplined spending.
He describes his housing approach as practical and includes protection for renters among his priorities.
He calls for reconsidering parts of the Official Community Plan because he says its population forecasts are outdated.

name: Susan Kim

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on Victoria For All launch

biography: Kim has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. Her City biography describes a decade of work in food security, community organizing, adult education, policy and operations, including roles in government and Island Health.

platform.summary: Victoria For All proposes doubling City investment in affordable housing; Kim appears as a candidate on the organization's shared platform.
The shared platform calls for expanded mental-health and addiction crisis response.
She supports expanding the tree canopy, improving the resilience of older rentals and using community centres for emergency cooling and response.
She calls for provincial flexibility that would let Victoria use more progressive forms of municipal taxation.

name: Krista Loughton
biography: Loughton has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. Her campaign and City biographies emphasize work on homelessness, mental health and addiction, alongside documentary filmmaking and community advocacy.

platform.summary: She promotes a rent-supplement and light-support model intended to help people move from supportive housing into market rentals, freeing supportive units for others.
Her campaign describes a goal of walkable, accessible and vibrant neighbourhoods under a 'City of Communities' theme.
She supports more non-profit and workforce housing, backed by additional provincial and federal funding.
She proposes regionalizing homelessness services, adding sober recovery housing and sharing policing and public-safety costs across the region.

name: Bella Lee

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on campaign launch

biography: Lee describes herself as a lifelong Victoria resident and renter with experience in community and political organizing. Her campaign says she advocated for the Crystal Pool referendum and is focused on affordability and public spaces.

platform.summary: She makes lowering the cost of living and improving housing affordability central campaign themes.
She calls for costs associated with homelessness to be shared regionally rather than concentrated in Victoria.
She supports investment in accessible public and recreation spaces, including the Crystal Pool replacement.

name: Arthur McInnis
biography: McInnis is a law professor and former international construction lawyer and tribunal member. His campaign biography says he brings more than 30 years of legal and governance experience to the race.

platform.summary: He proposes an integrity commissioner, a lobbyist registry, a civic-land inventory and public-facing performance dashboards.
He calls for zero-based budgeting and a 90-day public consultation before tax increases above inflation.
He supports pre-approved housing patterns, rental replacement and right-to-return rules, and long-term leases of public land.

name: Karen Rothe
biography: Rothe is a Vic West resident and career British Columbia public servant. Her campaign biography describes work on Metro Vancouver's regional growth strategy, wildfire evacuation policy and search-and-rescue funding.

platform.summary: She emphasizes transparent decisions, listening and clear council responsibility for outcomes.
She proposes a coordinated downtown revival effort that includes neighbourhood associations and local businesses.
She says the City should prioritize core responsibilities, including infrastructure, transportation, safety and affordability, using data-informed planning.

name: Jack Sandor

statusSource.label: Victoria Buzz report on campaign launch

biography: Sandor is a Red Seal electrician who grew up in Victoria's Gonzales neighbourhood. His campaign biography describes construction work on market and subsidized housing, health facilities and other major projects, as well as housing and transportation advocacy.

platform.summary: He places housing supply and affordability at the centre of his council campaign.
He argues for reliable public services and infrastructure informed by practical construction experience.
His campaign identifies stronger support for local businesses as a priority.

name: Dave Thompson
biography: Thompson has served on Victoria City Council since 2022. His campaign biography describes a background in public service, environmental work and community volunteering.

platform.summary: He supports more affordable rental housing, additional provincial and federal investment, and faster approvals for affordable and other housing.
He calls for a health-and-housing response to homelessness while linking safer streets with support for vulnerable neighbours.
Climate action is listed among the priorities for his developing re-election platform.

name: Owen Haley
biography: Haley is publicly listed for the 2026 Victoria council race by Livable CRD. No candidate-owned biography or campaign website was located in the initial research snapshot.
